advisory.finding: The poison-pill/ceiling test asserts only that the cursor advanced past 4900, but never asserts the `RECONCILE_DEGRADED reason=holdback_expired` marker was emitted. The docstring for `_persist_cursor` and the change message state the whole point of the ceiling is that the stuck change is 'surfaced loudly instead of being dropped in silence' via this greppable marker (carrying the offending `change_ids`). A regression that removed the `_degraded("holdback_expired", ...)` call — leaving the cursor clamp intact — would still pass this test, so the observability contract that justifies the ceiling is regression-blind.
scenarios: A refactor removes or mis-guards the `_degraded("holdback_expired")` call while keeping the cursor clamp; the stuck change is silently dropped again — the exact regression 9f63 fixed — yet the suite stays green.

advisory.finding: The events-log check-error hold-back branch is untested. When `gc.has_llm_review_vote` raises `GerritError`, reconcile.py adds the candidate to `held_back` and holds the cursor back (a distinct retryable trigger from timeout and voter error/deferred). No test drives `has_llm_review_vote` to raise, so this hold-back path — one of the three trigger classes the change message enumerates ('an events-log check error, a review timeout, or a voter error/deferred result') — has no regression coverage.
scenarios: A GerritError during the pre-check no longer holds the cursor back (e.g. the `held_back[change_id] = ev_time` line is dropped in a refactor); a candidate whose vote-existence check errored falls out of the next window forever, the original 9f63 failure mode for the check-error trigger, with a green suite.

dropped.finding: A retryably-abandoned candidate whose event time resolves to 0 (missing/zero eventCreatedOn AND missing/zero patchSet.createdOn) is dropped from `floors` in `_persist_cursor`, so the cursor advances to `newest` and the candidate falls outside every future `?t1=` window with no hold-back and no degraded marker — the same silent-loss mode bug 9f63 targets.
scenarios: An events-log entry lacking eventCreatedOn and patchSet.createdOn that the voter defers or errors on
